 #5
Price in any market partly moves because of the sentiment. To put simply if enough people think price is going down, then it will drop and if enough people think it is going up, then it will rise. So it is not the worse thing to look out the speculations and see what people are "feeling" at any particular time but it is not a strong reason to make decisions based on.

Take your own example with Strategy selling and the FUD that followed. Now open the charts and look at how it was changing in the past 3 months (basically since June 5). Do you see any difference? Or is the price in the same sideway trend going up and down between roughly $60k and $65k?

It's obviously the sideway market and we had a bigger initial range ($57k to $67k) which got tighter as time passed and we are stuck in this accumulation phase. Price isn't exactly going down to test its bottom because of some negative news and it doesn't necessarily going up to test its top because of  some positive news.

Quote from: Cryptohygenic on August 17, 2026, 11:41:55 PM
investors will begin sell out of Fomo
I think the term F.O.M.O. that stands for Fear Of Missing Out is only used for "panic buying" not "panic selling"

If you want to become more confused in your crypto journey, just continue following speculation, it will mess with your mental health. Understand that there are many factors that causes the price to experience upwards and downwards movement, not only from buying and selling pressure.

Quote
Was it not just last week with the news that Strategy sold 1,690 of bitcoin for approximately $104.7 million? Then speculations with negative odds about how bitcoin price was going to be negatively affected continued to erupt with the believe that other investors will begin sell out of Fomo and wants to opt out before the margin sells begin to have effect in the market.
I think you wanted to say "FUD" but you ended saying FOMO  
This is not the first time that Strategy is selling their bitcoins and it didn't reflect market sentiment. This is why it is not good to follow speculation from people because sometimes, the market doesn't work the way people are picturing it. As Strategy is selling their bitcoins, some investors are making huge purchases thereby creating a support in the price of bitcoin, that is why it didn't have any negative impact in the price.

Quote
And currently the market even looks like it has gained some supports to break the long time $65,000 resistance. Meanwhile Strategy sold when the market was trading at $63,000.
Don't be surprised that the market is gaining despite the selling pressure from Strategy, there might be inflow that you are not aware of.

Giving too much attention to the market is not a too welcome thing to do , because it can not change anything when it comes to the price of bitcoin.

Paying attention to speculations that might possibly have some effects on the market is totally worth it, but it's not worth paying too much attention to everything, which basically means that we should have enough knowledge and understanding to keep an eye on important events and speculations and don't give much importance to things that we know are not going to do much. Someone with enough experience should know that a specific news or maybe a prediction made by someone is going to or not going to have a positive or negative effect on the market.

So many people mostly pay too much attention to almost every single thing they see or hear about the industry that people are saying or doing, and they even make or sometimes change their investment decisions based on this, which shouldn't be the case. If you let any news or speculation affect your financial decisions, you will basically just act as a controlled toy that anyone can use to manipulate the market, because it's a combination of such people that allows whales to turn prices around and benefit from that.
